title: Stability channel matrix and safe upgrade paths for runtime, API, SDKs, and Console
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define pragmatic channel definitions (Stable / Extended Stable / Developer Preview), a cross-surface support matrix (runtime, REST API, Python SDK, Node SDK, Console) and concrete automated upgrade and rollback paths that preserve customer SLOs and minimize operational toil.
goals: 1) Unify channel semantics across surfaces so a channel name implies a set of guarantees. 2) Provide an explicit mapping of supported version pairings for runtime <-> API <-> SDK <-> Console. 3) Deliver a scripted upgrade tool + canary rollout gates integrated with Console that automates safe rollouts and rollbacks.
non_goals: We are not redesigning semantic versioning itself or changing existing public API endpoints in this ticket. Non-backwards-compatible API changes are out of scope and will require separate deprecation cycle tickets.
support_matrix:
Columns: Surface | Stable | Extended Stable (ES) | Dev Preview
Runtime | runtime-1.x (security/bugfix only) | runtime-0.9.x + security backports for 6 months | runtime-main nightlies for early testing
REST API | v1 (backwards-compatible patches only) | v1.x with compatibility shims for 3 months | v2-preview (feature flags on)
Python SDK | py-1.x (pinned to v1 API) | py-0.9.x (ES patches) | py-main (alpha)
Node SDK | node-1.x | node-0.9.x | node-canary
Console | console-2025.stable | console-2024.es (security-only) | console-alpha (feature flags)
Notes: ES channel receives security fixes and critical bug fixes only; Stable receives GA patch releases and security fixes. Dev Preview may break compatibility and has no SLA.
versioning_policy: We keep semantic versioning for public SDKs and runtime components. Channel labels map to allowed version ranges. Example rule: Stable = major X for SDKs/runtime where we guarantee no behaviour-changing patches within X+1 months without a deprecation process. Extended Stable = previous major with security-only backports for defined window. Dev Preview = CI-driven builds, no guarantees.
upgrade_strategy_summary: 1) Preflight (automated compatibility checks, smoke tests, token-limited dry runs). 2) Canary (1% traffic to new channel variant, 60m observation). 3) Gradual ramp (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with metric gates). 4) Verification (post-rollout health checks). 5) Postmortem/retro if any gate trips. Automated rollback on gate failures.
rollout_gates:
- Functional tests: all core smoke tests must pass in canary cluster.
- Latency SLO: p95 must not regress > 10% relative to baseline.
- Error budget: error rate must stay within configured budget (default 0.1% for Stable).
- Cost delta: per-token cost increase must be < 15% for Stable.
- Quality regressions: automated eval prompts (sample set) must not drop more than 2 points on our rubric.
Gates are codified in console/rollouts and are evaluated every 5m during canary windows.
automation_tasks:
- release-engineering: build 'channel-upgrade' CLI to coordinate preflight, canary, ramp, rollback. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-tools/pull/412)
- infra: add canary routing flag and traffic-split API (RFC merged: https://confluence.redwood.ai/r/ChannelRoutingRFC)
- console: rollout UI to display channel health and allow manual override (ticket CON-2213).
migration_plan:
Phase 0: Docs & tooling (this ticket) + customer communication templates.
Phase 1: Stabilize channel definitions, publish support_matrix doc and compatibility checker.
Phase 2: Pilot with internal services (search service, embeddings ingestion).
Phase 3: Opt-in public customers (beta).
Phase 4: Promote to Stable and update general availability docs.
Each phase includes a rollback rehearsal exercise and at least one post-rehearsal retrospective.
acceptance_criteria:
- Published channel definitions page in Confluence and public docs.
- Support matrix committed as markdown in docs repo.
- 'channel-upgrade' CLI merged with e2e tests.
- Canary gating integrated into Console and tested with synthetic traffic.
- Pilot rollout executed with internal service and documented lessons learned.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Customers may be confused by channel names - Mitigation: ship customer-facing FAQ and map legacy LTS terminology to new channels.
Risk: Automation rollback may not cover DB schema mismatches - Mitigation: require schema compatibility checks in preflight.
Risk: SDK pinning complexity - Mitigation: provide compatibility-checker script and CI badge for supported pairings.
notes:
Decision: prefer preserving current public API endpoints; we will use feature flags for API surface changes.
Tradeoff: Using 'Extended Stable' reduces release velocity for older majors but improves enterprise reliability.
Feedback: PMs asked for explicit calendar for ES windows; agreed to publish a 6-month ES window per major.
